full_caption: Ottoline Ingleside, Appellant, v. Jasper Grimsby-Hale, Appellee
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: Ottoline Ingleside, the association governing the Stonebrook subdivision, brought this action to enjoin Jasper Grimsby-Hale from maintaining a detached structure at 2485 Ferndale Road, Cobbleton, AR in violation of Article III of the recorded declaration.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: The defense of changed conditions requires a showing that the character of the neighborhood has so altered that the original purpose of the restriction can no longer be achieved. Isolated violations elsewhere in the subdivision do not meet that standard.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: The association's architectural review committee denied the application by letter dated February 5, 2013. The declaration requires that denials state the specific ground relied upon; the letter recited only that the proposal was 'not in harmony with the community.'

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: Covenants are construed in favor of the free use of land. Ambiguity in a restriction is resolved against the party seeking to enforce it, and a restriction will not be extended by implication to conduct not fairly within its terms.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: The association waived enforcement as to fence height by failing to act against 11 comparable violations over a period of 21 years. Selective enforcement of a covenant against one owner, after acquiescence in like violations by others, is inequitable.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: Article III prohibits 'any outbuilding, shed or accessory structure exceeding one hundred twenty square feet.' The structure erected by Jasper Grimsby-Hale measures 820 square feet and is therefore within the plain reach of the restriction.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: Assessments levied under Article VIII became a lien on the lot upon recording of the notice of assessment. The lien is subordinate to a first mortgage recorded earlier in time but superior to subsequent encumbrances.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: Fines totaling $250 were imposed without the hearing required by the bylaws. A fine imposed in disregard of the association's own procedural requirements is void, without regard to the merits of the underlying violation.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: Restrictive covenants are enforceable servitudes running with the land where they are (1) in writing, (2) intended to run, (3) touching and concerning the land, and (4) recorded so as to give notice to successors.

sections.heading: Paragraph 10
sections.text: The business judgment rule shields the board's maintenance and budgeting decisions from judicial second-guessing where the board acted within its authority, on an informed basis, and in the honest belief that the action served the association.

sections.heading: Paragraph 11
sections.text: A discretionary architectural approval power must be exercised reasonably and in good faith. A denial that states no articulable standard is arbitrary and will not support injunctive relief.

sections.heading: Paragraph 12
sections.text: We reverse the injunction as to the fence and affirm as to the accessory structure. The award of fines is vacated in its entirety.

sections.heading: RIDER 2 — ASSESSMENTS, LIENS AND PRIORITY
sections.text: Annual assessments are levied against each Lot in equal shares and are due on the first day of each fiscal year. Unpaid assessments bear interest at 9 percent per annum and become a lien upon recording of a notice of assessment lien in the Cobbleton County land records. The lien is subordinate to a first mortgage of record predating the notice and superior to all other subsequently recorded encumbrances. The Association shall furnish an estoppel statement of amounts due within 3 days of written request.

sections.heading: RIDER 3 — ENFORCEMENT, FINES AND HEARING RIGHTS
sections.text: Before imposing any fine, the Board shall give the owner written notice of the alleged violation and an opportunity to be heard before the Board or a committee of at least three members who are not officers. Fines shall not exceed $250 per violation nor $1,000 in the aggregate for a continuing violation. A fine imposed without the notice and hearing required by this Rider is void.

sections.heading: RIDER 4 — LEASING RESTRICTION
sections.text: No Lot may be leased for a term of less than 9 months, and no more than 6 percent of the Lots may be leased at any one time. An owner in possession on the date this Rider was recorded is exempt as to that Lot until title is transferred. This Rider does not apply to a lease to a family member of the owner or to occupancy incident to a mortgagee's possession following foreclosure.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Indemnity
sections.text: Each party shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless the other from all claims, damages and expenses, including reasonable attorney's fees, arising out of that party's use of the subject premises or breach of this instrument, except to the extent caused by the negligence or willful misconduct of the party seeking indemnity. This clause survives termination.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Counterparts and Electronic Signature
sections.text: This instrument may be executed in counterparts, each of which is an original and all of which together constitute one instrument. A signature delivered electronically has the same effect as an original, provided that any instrument submitted for recording shall bear original signatures and acknowledgment before a notary public of the State of Ardenne.

sections.heading: Clause 3 — Entire Agreement and Riders
sections.text: This instrument, together with the exhibits and riders attached and incorporated by reference, constitutes the entire agreement of the parties and supersedes all prior negotiations, representations and agreements, whether oral or written. In the event of a conflict between a printed provision and a rider, the rider shall control, the rider being the specifically negotiated expression of the parties' intent.

sections.heading: Clause 4 — Attorney's Fees
sections.text: In any action to enforce or construe this instrument, the prevailing party shall recover its reasonable attorney's fees, expert fees and costs, at trial and on appeal. Where the instrument grants fees to one party only, this clause shall be read as reciprocal and shall entitle the other party to fees on the same terms if that party prevails.
